name: Brendan the Navigator's Atlantic voyage (traditional)
summary: Traditional dating of the Irish abbot Brendan of Clonfert's (c. 484–c. 577) seven-year Atlantic voyage in search of the 'Isle of the Blessed'. The 9th-century Navigatio Sancti Brendani Abbatis, which fictionalises and elaborates the journey, became one of the most-copied Latin texts of the central Middle Ages and was read by Columbus before 1492.

_quarry.structural_significance: Foundation of the Latin Christian imaginative geography of the Atlantic, the Hy-Brasil, Saint Brendan's Isle, and Antillia appearing on 13th–15th-century portolan charts trace to this tradition. Modern voyages in skin currachs (Severin 1976) demonstrated the Atlantic journey is technically achievable in 6th-century craft.
